Title: Provision of a Medical Advisory Service for Scottish Public Pension Agency
Reference: SPPA/2030-03/2026/057
Buying organisation: Scottish Public Pensions Agency
Published: 2026-11-18
Closing: 2027-01-06
Procurement category: services
Classification: Health and social work services
Description: Provision of a Medical Advisory Service to support the Contracting Authority’s activities in administering the National Health Service (NHS) and Teachers’ pension schemes in Scotland and determining the Local Government Pension Scheme (Scotland)’s (LGPS) Internal Disputes Resolution Procedure (IDRP)’s appeals. For the period 01 April 2027 to 31 March 2030. The Contracting Authority may, by giving notice to the Economic Operator, extend the period of the contract to a date falling no later than 31 March 2032. Subject to that constraint, the Contracting Authority may extend the period of the Contract on more than one occasion.

NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that the Council of the Royal Borough of Greenwich (hereinafter referred to as “the Council”) proposes to make the above-mentioned Orders under sections 6, 45, 46, 49, 124 and Part IV of Schedule 9 of the Road Traffic Regulation Act 1984, as amended. 2. The general effect of the Orders would be to: a) to replace 2.5 metres to 3 metres of various existing control where appropriate with a secure bicycle parking facility (cycle hangar) in each of the following locations: i. Allenby Road, north-east side, from a point 16.95 metres south-east of the south-eastern building line of No.2 Allenby Road in a north-westerly direction replacing ‘No waiting at any time’ restrictions; Annandale Road, west side, from a point 6 metres south of the southern property boundary of No. 85 Annandale Road in a southerly direction, replacing part of the ‘Residents and Business Permit Holders Only Mon-Fri 9am-6.30pm Zone W’ bay; Bowater Place, east side, from a point 5 metres south of the southern property boundary of No. 2 Bowater Place in a southerly direction, replacing part of the ‘Free Parking Place’ restriction; Bramhope Lane, east side, from a point 4.5 metres south of the northern building line of Victor House in a northerly direction, replacing part of the ‘Free Parking Place’; Calydon Road, north-west side, from a point 4 metres south-west of the common boundary of Nos. 11 and 13 Calydon Road in a north-easterly direction replacing ‘No Waiting Mon-Sat 9am-6.30pm’ restrictions; Church Manorway, east side, from a point 11.8 metres south of the southern building line of No.2 Church Manorway in a northerly direction, replacing ‘No Waiting Mon-Sat 8am-6.30pm’ restrictions; Deptford Green, west side, from a point 5.1 metres south of its junction with Borthwick Street in a southerly direction, replacing part of the ‘Limited Waiting 1 Hour No Return 30 Mins Mon-Fri 12pm-2pm’ bay; Earlswood Street, north-east side, from a point 7.8 metres north-west of the north-western property boundary of No. 27 Earlswood Street in a north-westerly direction, replacing part of the ‘Permit Holders Only 9am-6.30pm Zone EG’ bay; Egerton Drive, west side, from a point 5.8 metres south of its junction with Ashburnham Place in a southerly direction, replacing part of the ‘Residents and Business Permit Holders Only Mon-Sat 9am-5pm and Sun 9am-6pm Zone G’ restrictions; Eversley Road, south side, from a point 14.65 metres west of the eastern property boundary of No. 19 Wyndcliff Road in an easterly direction, replacing part of the ‘Permit Holders or Limited Waiting Mon-Sat 9am-6.30pm Max stay 2 Hours No return within 3 hours Zone C’ bay; Eversley Road, south side, from a point 14.5 metres west of the western building line of No.2 Eversley Road in a westerly direction, replacing ‘No waiting at any time’ restrictions; Grangehill Road, south-west side, from a point 22 metres north-west of its junction with Greenvale Road in a north-westerly direction, replacing ‘Free Parking Place’ and ‘No Waiting Mon-Fri 11am-12.30pm’ restrictions; Gurdon Road, south side, from a point 8.9 metres west of the eastern property boundary of No. 30 Dupree Road in a westerly direction, replacing part of the ‘Permit Holders or Limited Waiting Mon-Sat 9am-6.30pm Max stay 2 Hours No return within 3 hours Zone C’ bay; Humber Road, north-west side, from a point 14 metres south-west of the south-western property boundary of No. 55 Humber Road in a south-westerly direction, replacing ‘No Waiting Mon-Sat 9am-6.30pm’ and ‘Cycle Hire Parking Place’ restrictions; Kirkside Road, south side, from a point 3.5 metres west of the common boundary of Nos. 37 and 39 Kirkside Road in an easterly direction, replacing part of the ‘Permit Holders or Limited Waiting Mon-Sat 9am-6.30pm Max stay 2 Hours No return within 3 hours Zone W’ bay; Lyveden Road, north side, from a point 6.9 metres west of its junction with Furzefield Road in a westerly direction, replacing part of the ‘Permit Holders or Limited Waiting Mon-Sat 9am-6.30pm Max stay 2 Hours No return within 3 hours Zone C’ bay; Owenite Street, west side, from a point 11.65 metres north of the northern property boundary of No.2 Owenite Street in a northerly direction, replacing part of the ‘Permit Holders Only Mon-Fri 11am-1pm Zone AW’ bay; Point Hill, south-west side, from a point 12.4 metres north of the northern kerbline of Point Close for 3 metres in a northerly direction replacing ‘No waiting at any time’ restrictions and part of a ‘Cycle Hire Parking Place’; The Heights, north side, from a point 6.6 metres west of the eastern building line of No. 27a and 27b The Heights in a westerly direction, replacing part of the ‘Free Parking Place’ and ‘No Waiting Mon-Sat 9am-6.30pm’

Transport for London, hereby gives notice that it intends to make the above named Order under section 6 of the Road Traffic Regulation Act 1984. 2. The general nature and effect of the Order will be to: (1) shorten the 30 metre long Monday to Saturday 7am to 7pm parking 30 minute No return 1 hour bay outside Nos. 13 to 23 Lewisham Road by 14 metres to accommodate an 11.5 metre long at any time hireable cycle bay bracketed by 1.2 metre traffic islands at each end. A double red line (No Stopping at Any Time) restriction will be introduced to accommodate the change; (2) shorten the 16 metre long Monday to Saturday 7am to 7pm parking 1 hour No return 2 hours bay at the north-eastern kerb of Arbroath Road outside Nos. 179 and 181 Well Hall Road by 10.5 metres to accommodate an 8.2 metre long at any time hireable cycle bay with a 1.4 metre traffic islands at its north-western end. The adjacent double red line (No Stopping at Any Time) restriction will be adjusted to accommodate the change; (3) replace the Monday to Saturday 7am to 7pm Parking 1 hour No return 2 hours bay at the western kerb of Cobbett Road at the side of St Barnabas Church, Rochester Way, with a 12 metre long at any time hireable cycle bay with a 1.2 metre traffic islands at its southern end. The adjacent double red line (No Stopping at Any Time) restriction will be adjusted to accommodate the change; (4) replace the Parking at Any Time bay at the northern kerb of Dickson Road at the side of No. 125 Well Hall Road with an 8 metre long at any time hireable cycle bay with a 1.2 metre traffic islands at its western end. The adjacent double red line (No Stopping at Any Time) restriction will be adjusted to accommodate the change; (5) shorten the 17 metre long Monday to Saturday 10am to 4pm loading 20 mins No return 40 minutes and Disabled Persons’ Vehicles 3 hours bay at the north-eastern kerb of Dunblane Road outside No. 369 Well Hall Road by 10.4 metres to accommodate an 9 metre long at any time hireable cycle bay with a 1.4 metre traffic islands its north-western end. The adjacent double red line (No Stopping at Any Time) restriction will be adjusted to accommodate the change; (6) replace the Monday to Saturday 7am to 7pm Parking 1 hour No return 2 hours bay at the north-eastern kerb of Legatt Road, at the side of No. 515 Westhorne Avenue, with a 9 metre long at any time hireable cycle bay with a 1.2 metre traffic island at its north-western end. A double red line (No Stopping at Any Time) restriction will be introduced to accommodate the change; (7) replace the Monday to Saturday 7am to 7pm Parking 1 hour No return 2 hours bay at the southern kerb of side road Well Hall Road, opposite No. 171 Well Hall Road, with a 9 metre long at any time hireable cycle bay with a 1.2 metre traffic island at its western end. The adjacent double red line (No Stopping at Any Time) restriction will be adjusted to accommodate the change; (8) make administrative changes to the controls on the Side Road Well Hall Road to correct historical errors. 3. The roads which would be affected by the Order are the A2 GLA side road Lewisham Road, the A205 GLA side roads Arbroath Road, Cobbett Road, Dickson Road, Dunblane Road, Legatt Road and Well Hall Road. 4. A copy of the Order, a statement of Transport for London’s reasons for the proposals, a map indicating the location and effect of the Order and copies of any Order revoked, suspended or varied by the Order can be inspected by visiting our website at https://haveyoursay.tfl.gov.uk/tro and selecting the relevant borough and reference the Traffic Order relates to or by appointment during normal office hours at our office at the address below. To arrange an appointment please email [contact removed] Copies of the documents may be requested via email at [contact removed], or by post at the following address quoting reference SNO/REGULATION/STOT/GK/TRO/GLA/2026/0650: • Transport for London, Streets Traffic Order Team (SNO/REGULATION/STOT), Palestra, 197 Blackfriars Road, London, SE1 8NJ. 5. All objections and other representations to the proposed Order must be made in writing and must specify the grounds on which they are made. Objections and representations must be sent to Transport for London, Streets Traffic Order Team, Palestra, 197 Blackfriars Road, London, SE1 8NJ or by emailing [contact removed] quoting reference SNO/REGULATION/STOT/GK/TRO/GLA/2026/0650, to arrive before 9th December 2026. Please note due to hybrid working access to post is restricted and requests for documents and confirmation of your objections or representations may be delayed. Objections and other representations may be communicated to other persons who may be affected. Dated this 18th day of November

NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that Westminster City Council on 16th November 2026 made the above Order under sections 6, 45, 46, 49, 63 and 124 of and Part IV of Schedule 9 to the Road Traffic Regulation Act 1984, as amended. 2. The general effect of the Order will be, in connection with improvements to the cycle routes on Lupus Street, to: (a) replace the residents’ parking place on the west side of Lupus Street, between Turpentine Lane and Westmoreland Terrace, with double yellow line “at any time” waiting restrictions; (b) introduce double yellow line “at any time” waiting restrictions on both sides of Lupus Street, on the bend opposite Westmoreland Terrace and Sussex Street; (c) replace the redundant doctor parking place on the south side of Lupus Street, outside Nash House, with a car club parking place; (d) relocate the cycle hangar and one electric vehicle parking bay from the north side of Lupus Street, at the rear of No. 96 Gloucester Street, to the south side of Lupus Street, outside Nash House (replacing the car club parking place); and (e) introduce a loading bay (operating between 7.00 a.m. and 7.00 p.m. throughout the week, with a maximum stay of 2 hours and no return within 1 hour) on the south side of Lupus Street, outside De Quincey House (replacing two pay-by-phone parking bays and a length of single yellow line waiting restrictions). An advisory with-flow cycle lane will also be introduced on the north side of Lupus Street, between Turpentine Lane and Westmoreland Terrace. 3. The Order, which will come into force on 23rd November 2026, and other documents giving more detailed particulars of the Order are available for inspection until 28th December 2026 at https://westminstertransportationservices.co.uk/notices and, in person by appointment only, at Westminster City Hall, 64 Victoria Street, London, SW1E 6QP, between 9.00 a.m. and 5.00 p.m. on Mondays to Fridays (except bank / public holidays). Please telephone 020 3116 9388 or email [contact removed] to arrange an appointment. 4. Any person desiring to question the validity of the Order or of any provision contained therein on the grounds that it is not within the relevant powers of the Road Traffic Regulation Act 1984 or that any of the relevant requirements thereof or of any relevant regulations made thereunder have not been complied with in relation to the Order may, within six weeks from the date on which the Order was made, make application for the purpose to the High Court. Dated 18th November 2026 JONATHAN ROWING, Head of Parking (The officer appointed for this purpose) Actions Save notice to My Gazette Remove from My Gazette Loading... NOTICE TO THE CREDITORS OF AN INSOLVENT COMPANY REGARDING THE RE-USE OF A PROHIBITED NAME RULE 22.4 OF THE INSOLVENCY (ENGLAND AND WALES) RULES 2016 COLOUR GRAPHICS LTD Registered Number: 04794437 Trading Name: Trading name or style: Colour Graphics / Fabrix Registered office: Azzurri House, Walsall Road, Aldridge, Walsall, WS9 0RB Principal trading address: Azzurri House, Walsall Road, Aldridge, Walsall, WS9 0RB On 15 October 2026 the above-named company went into insolvent liquidation. I, James Birch of 1 Heath Gap, Lichfield, WS13 8PH, was a director of the above-named company during the 12 months ending with the day before it went into liquidation. I give notice that it is my intention to act in all or any of the ways specified in section 216(3) of the Insolvency Act 1986 in connection with, or for the purposes of, the carrying on of the whole or substantially the whole of the business of the insolvent company under the following name: Printcorp Ltd t/a Colour Graphics; Printcorp Ltd t/a Fabrix. Rule 22.5 - Statement as to the effect of the notice under rule 22.4(2): “Section 216(3) of the Insolvency Act 1986 lists the activities that a director of a company that has gone into insolvent liquidation may not undertake unless the court gives permission or there is an exception in the Insolvency Rules made under the Insolvency Act 1986. (This includes the exceptions in Part 22 of the Insolvency (England and Wales) Rules 2016). These activities are- (a) acting as a director of another company that is known by a name which is either the same as a name used by the company in insolvent liquidation in the 12 months before it entered liquidation or is so similar as to suggest an association with that company; (b) directly or indirectly being concerned or taking part in the promotion, formation or management of any such company; or (c) directly or indirectly being concerned in the carrying on of a business otherwise than through a company under a name of the kind mentioned in (a) above. This notice is given under rule 22.4 of the Insolvency (England and Wales) Rules 2016 where the business of a company which is in, or may go into, insolvent liquidation is, or is to be, carried on otherwise than by the company in liquidation with the involvement of a director of that company and under the same or a similar name to that of that company. The purpose of the giving of this notice is to permit the director to act in these circumstances where the company enters (or has entered) insolvent liquidation without the director committing a criminal offence and in the case of the carrying on of the business through another company, being personally liable for that company’s debts. Notice may be given where the person giving the notice is already the director of a company which proposes to adopt a prohibited name.” Notes: 1. This notice must be given to every creditor of the insolvent company whose name and address is known or is ascertainable on the making of such enquiries as are reasonable in the circumstances. 2. This notice must be published in the London Gazette. 3. The notice to creditors and the London Gazette must be given and published no later than 28 days after completion of the acquisition of the whole (or substantially the whole) of the business of the insolvent company under arrangements made by the liquidator or office holder acting as administrator, administrative receiver or supervisor of a CVA. text: Gareth Davies Appointed as New Home Office Permanent Secretary | Gareth is currently Permanent Secretary at the Department for Business and Trade. He has previously held senior roles across government in business, transport and Downing Street. He started his career in the private sector, and has worked across Europe and south east Asia. Gareth set up the Department for Business and Trade and has led it over the last three years. During this time, the department secured major trade deals including with India and the United States, landed major investments, hosted the International Investment Summit, launched the Industrial Strategy, and passed the Employment Rights Act. Home Secretary, the Rt Hon Shabana Mahmood MP, said: Gareth Davies brings decades of experience in senior government and private sector roles, and a strong record of delivery supporting British trade and industry and transforming departments. I look forward to working with Gareth as we drive forward the most significant reforms to policing and migration in generations, and deliver our mission to keep the British public safe and restore order to our borders. I would also like to thank Dame Antonia Romeo for her exceptional leadership of the department, and Simon Ridley for his valuable counsel while serving as Acting Permanent Secretary in recent months. Cabinet Secretary, Dame Antonia Romeo, said: This is an important appointment for the Home Office and the Civil Service. Gareth is a brilliant permanent secretary who brings a wealth of experience of delivery and innovation from the public and private sectors. The Home Office is charged with delivery of some of the Government’s highest priorities, and Gareth is strongly suited to grip delivery and productivity in support of the Home Secretary and the Prime Minister. I would also like to thank Simon Ridley for his strong leadership of the department in the interim period. Gareth Davies CB said: It’s an honour to be appointed Permanent Secretary of the Home Office - one of the great offices of state. There’s no more important agenda in government than keeping the country safe and secure. I’m looking forward to working with the amazing team of civil servants to deliver the Home Secretary’s priorities and build a department that is even more innovative and productive. I would like to thank the incredible team at the Department of Business and Trade. They should be very proud of the difference they make to the lives of families and communities across our country. The appointment has been agreed by the First Civil Service Commissioner and the Prime Minister. Gareth Davies will start as Home Office Permanent Secretary on the 6th April. Amanda Brooks CBE has been appointed Interim Permanent Secretary at the Department for Business and Trade. Amanda is currently Director General for Trade at the Department and has a wealth of experience in senior government roles covering domestic and international economic policy.
title: Gareth Davies Appointed as New Home Office Permanent Secretary

text: Tom Riordan Appointed as New Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government | The Cabinet Secretary, with the approval of the Prime Minister, has appointed Tom Riordan as the new Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government (MHCLG). Tom is currently the Northern Growth Envoy. He has previously been Second Permanent Secretary and Chief Operating Officer at the Department of Health and Social Care, and before that was Chief Executive of Leeds City Council. Angela Rayner, Secretary of State for Housing, Communities & Local Government, said: Few people have done more than Tom Riordan to champion devolution, good growth and strong local leadership - which makes him the perfect appointment at a critical time. I’m delighted he’s joining MHCLG and look forward to working with him as we get on with building the homes we need, improving local places and giving communities more control over their future. I’d also like to thank Dame Sarah Healey for her leadership of the department and Will Garton for his support as Interim Permanent Secretary in recent months. Cabinet Secretary, Dame Antonia Romeo, said: I am delighted to announce Tom’s appointment as Permanent Secretary for MHCLG. Tom’s wealth of experience in central and local government, combined with his time as the Northern Growth Envoy and CEO of Leeds City Council, makes him ideally suited to lead MHCLG’s crucial policy agenda delivering devolution and growth in every postcode. I would also like to thank Will Garton for his leadership of the department in the interim period. Tom Riordan said: It’s a privilege to be taking up such an important job to help ensure the whole country benefits from more affordable and safe homes, well run public services and strong regional growth. This feels like the right job at the right time as the Government devolves power, given how much I’ve valued working in local and regional government, and applying that learning to improving national policy. The appointment follows an internal recruitment exercise chaired by the independent First Civil Service Commissioner. Tom will start as MHCLG Permanent Secretary on 21 September. ENDS Notes to Editors: This is a Permanent Secretary level appointment, offered on a fixed term basis for five years. Tom is currently Northern Growth Envoy, based in HM Treasury. Prior to that he was Second Permanent Secretary and Chief Operating Officer at DHSC and was CEO of Leeds City Council between 2010 and 2024.
title: Tom Riordan Appointed as New Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government

text: Clara Swinson appointed as Second Permanent Secretary at the Ministry of Justice | The appointment has been made with the approval of the Prime Minister and Deputy Prime Minister. Her appointment is part of the government’s plan to reform the justice system. As Second Permanent Secretary, she will provide leadership across the Criminal Justice System in taking forward the government’s response to Sir Brian Leveson’s Independent Review of the Criminal Courts. Clara is currently Second Permanent Secretary in the Cabinet Office. The Secretary of State for Justice and the Deputy Prime Minister, the Rt Hon. David Lammy said: I am pleased that Clara Swinson is joining the Ministry of Justice bringing her extensive experience to this role. I look forward to working with Clara to deliver our plan for faster and fairer justice for victims by combining investment, reform, and modernisation. Permanent Secretary MOJ, Dr Jo Farrar said: I am delighted to welcome Clara to the Ministry of Justice. Clara brings a wealth of experience, of working across systems, both from her current role in the Cabinet Office and her time at the Department of Health and Social Care. I look forward to working with her in the Ministry of Justice. Clara Swinson said: I am very pleased to be joining the Ministry of Justice at such a critical time and taking forward the government’s response to Sir Brian Leveson’s important recommendations for the criminal justice system. Clara will take up her new post in April 2026.
title: Clara Swinson appointed as Second Permanent Secretary at the Ministry of Justice
